name: Bell Labs eight-bit CCD shift register
description: Bell Labs built a three-phase CCD that clocked charge packets along eight stages and sensed them at an output diode. The team operated it with electrically injected charge as a serial shift register and used the same device as a rudimentary optical line scanner. The imaging output was displayed on an oscilloscope.

events.statement: Tompsett, Amelio and Smith reported an integrated eight-bit CCD operating as a shift register and as an optical line imager.

evidence.supports: Dates the report and identifies the 26-capacitor device, electrical charge injection and separate line imaging operation.
Shows the three-phase CCD with input and output diodes and reproduces its optical image on an oscilloscope.
The independent RCA account corroborates the early eight-stage class and describes three-phase serial transfer.

events.caveats: The publication dates the report. The precise image capture date is unresolved. Eight bits describes the register length.

earliest_record.rationale: The contemporary publication explicitly reports both operating modes of this integrated prototype.

links.statement: The integrated register implemented the Boyle–Smith concept by clocking charge packets along successive potential wells. It used integrated input and output diodes.
links.caveats: The April MOS capacitor verification measured charge transfer between electrodes in a different test structure.

evidence.supports: Describes coupled semiconductor charge storage, serial transfer and possible imaging.
Explicitly identifies the charge-coupled device concept as the basis for the integrated shift register.
The participant recounts the construction sequence from the charge-transfer test to the integrated register.
The independent RCA account describes the concept and its operation as a register, and situates the early eight-stage devices.
